grammar: Doe begins the main instruction and dit is its object. In the voordat-clause, subject je precedes the final finite verb vertrekt. Doe is the imperative of doen. Dit points independently to the indicated task. Voordat introduces a subordinate time clause. Vertrekt retains -t because je precedes the verb inside that clause.
variation: Doe dit voordat je naar huis gaat.

dutch: We hadden het boekjaar al afgesloten.
english: We'd already closed the financial year.
cue: When a late invoice arrived, the accounts team had already closed the financial year.
scenario: When a late invoice arrived, the accounts team had already closed the financial year.
grammar: We is first and hadden second; the object and al stand before afgesloten. Afsluiten is separable: sluiten af; its participle is afgesloten, with ge- inserted after af. Boekjaar is a het-word inherited from jaar. Past perfect hadden afgesloten puts closing the accounts before another past event.
variation: Zij hadden het boekjaar al afgesloten.

dutch: Ik denk na over het doel.
english: I'm thinking carefully about the goal.
cue: You pause to consider what a new project should actually achieve before planning its details.
scenario: You pause to consider what a new project should actually achieve before planning its details.
grammar: Ik comes first and denk second. The separated particle na appears before the over-phrase describing the topic. Nadenken is separable: ik denk na. Nadenken over means reflect on. Doel is a het-word. The present expresses current reflection; na belongs to the verb and is not the time preposition after here.
variation: We denken na over het doel.

dutch: Ik blijf hier staan.
cue: You keep standing beside a collection point while your colleague fetches the needed materials.
scenario: You keep standing beside a collection point while your colleague fetches the needed materials.
grammar: Ik is first and blijf second; hier locates the continuing posture, and staan is the final infinitive. Blijven + infinitive expresses continuing an activity or posture without te. Staan means stand; hier is a place adverb. Blijf has no -t with ik.
variation: Ik blijf hier zitten.

dutch: Ze praten over de kwaliteit, niet over de kleur.
english: They're talking about the quality, not the colour.
cue: Colleagues compare the workmanship of product samples rather than their different colours.
scenario: Colleagues compare the workmanship of product samples rather than their different colours.
grammar: Ze is first and praten second. A second over-phrase contrasts the excluded topic after niet. Plural praten makes ze mean they. Over introduces a conversation topic. Niet can negate a whole prepositional phrase for an explicit contrast. Kwaliteit and kleur are de-words.
variation: Ze praten over de kwaliteit, niet over de prijs.

dutch: Laat me even kijken.
english: Let me have a quick look.
cue: You ask for a brief moment to inspect a colleague’s document before answering a question.
scenario: You ask for a brief moment to inspect a colleague’s document before answering a question.
grammar: Laat begins the request; me is the person who will look, even softens the request, and kijken is final. Laten takes an infinitive without te. Me is an object form in the main clause and the understood subject of kijken. Even here means for a brief moment and softens the request, not the English adjective even.
variation: Laat me even naar de tekening kijken.

dutch: Ons bedrijf waardeert diversiteit.
cue: Colleagues with different backgrounds contribute ideas during an inclusive team discussion.
scenario: Colleagues with different backgrounds contribute ideas during an inclusive team discussion.
grammar: Ons bedrijf is first and waardeert is second; diversiteit is the object. Bedrijf is a singular het-word, so our is ons. The singular company requires waardeert with -t. Diversiteit is an abstract noun used without an article here. Waarderen means value/appreciate.
variation: Onze organisatie waardeert diversiteit.

dutch: Dat is zijn computer.
cue: You identify which workstation belongs to a particular colleague.
scenario: You identify which workstation belongs to a particular colleague.
grammar: Dat is the subject, is is second, and zijn computer identifies the object being pointed out. Dat stands independently; it does not have to agree with de computer. Zijn is possessive before computer, not the verb zijn. A possessive replaces the article.
variation: Dat is haar computer.

dutch: Kun je even praten?
english: Can you talk for a moment?
cue: You ask a colleague whether they have a moment for a private conversation.
scenario: You ask a colleague whether they have a moment for a private conversation.
grammar: Kun starts the yes/no question, subject je follows it, and praten is the final infinitive. Kun je is an informal inverted form. Even softens the request and suggests a brief conversation. Praten after kunnen is an infinitive without te. This context asks about availability rather than physical speech ability.
variation: Kun je straks even praten?

dutch: Ze is blij met haar nieuwe baan.
english: She's happy with her new job.
cue: A colleague happily describes her new workplace after changing jobs.
scenario: A colleague happily describes her new workplace after changing jobs.
grammar: Ze comes first and is second; blij is followed by met and the thing she is happy with. Blij zijn met is the normal combination for satisfaction with something. Haar is possessive. Baan is a de-word, so the adjective is nieuwe. The singular is makes ze mean she.
variation: Ze is blij met haar nieuwe collega’s.

dutch: Hij stuurde mij een e-mail.
cue: You tell a colleague that someone contacted you directly by email.
scenario: You tell a colleague that someone contacted you directly by email.
grammar: Hij is first and stuurde second. Recipient mij comes before the full object een e-mail. Stuurde is singular simple past of sturen. Mij is a stressed recipient object form; me is also possible. The indirect object does not require aan when placed before the direct object here.
variation: Hij stuurde me een e-mail.

dutch: Ze hebben je een brief geschreven.
english: They have written you a letter.
cue: You tell a colleague that several people have jointly written a letter addressed to them.
scenario: You tell a colleague that several people have jointly written a letter addressed to them.
grammar: Ze is first and hebben second. Recipient je and the letter stand before final geschreven. Hebben geschreven is a perfect. Schrijven has irregular participle geschreven. Je is an object recipient here, not possessive, because it is not a determiner of een brief. Plural hebben makes ze mean they.
variation: Ze hebben u een brief geschreven.

dutch: Kleding kopen is duur.
cue: You compare the cost of replacing a work wardrobe while browsing clothing racks.
scenario: You compare the cost of replacing a work wardrobe while browsing clothing racks.
grammar: The whole activity Kleding kopen is the first constituent. Is is second, followed by the predicate duur. Kleding is an uncountable collective noun in Dutch. The infinitive phrase is a singular activity subject. Duur is predicative without -e. The object kleding comes before the infinitive kopen inside the subject phrase.
variation: Nieuwe kleding kopen is duur.

dutch: Ze zullen u bellen zodra de bestelling klaar is.
english: They'll call you as soon as the order is ready.
cue: A shop employee explains that colleagues will telephone the customer when the order can be collected.
scenario: A shop employee explains that colleagues will telephone the customer when the order can be collected.
grammar: Ze zullen starts the main clause; u is the person called and bellen closes its verb group. In the zodra-clause, the finite is follows the subject and klaar. Zullen agrees with plural ze, not object u. Zodra means as soon as and introduces a subordinate clause. Klaar is a predicate adjective with no -e. The time clause follows the main infinitive naturally.
variation: Ze zullen u bellen zodra het pakket klaar is.

dutch: Wat was zijn feedback?
cue: After a colleague’s review, you ask what the reviewer said about the work.
scenario: After a colleague’s review, you ask what the reviewer said about the work.
grammar: Wat asks for the content; was is second and zijn feedback follows as the subject phrase. Was is singular past of zijn. Zijn is possessive before feedback. Feedback is normally uncountable in this use; the possessive supplies the determiner.
variation: Wat was haar feedback?

dutch: Deel alstublieft uw scherm.
cue: During a video call, you politely ask another participant to show their screen to the group.
scenario: During a video call, you politely ask another participant to show their screen to the group.
grammar: Deel starts the imperative, alstublieft makes the request polite, and uw scherm is the object. The ordinary imperative is the stem deel. Uw is the polite possessive before scherm; u is a personal pronoun. Het scherm is a het-word, but a possessive replaces the article. Scherm delen has the digital sharing meaning here.
variation: Deel alstublieft het juiste venster.

dutch: Zij heeft ons de borg teruggegeven.
english: She returned the deposit to us.
cue: After you return rented equipment, the rental worker refunds your deposit.
scenario: After you return rented equipment, the rental worker refunds your deposit.
grammar: Zij is first and heeft second. The short recipient ons precedes the full object de borg, followed by teruggegeven. Teruggeven uses hebben in the perfect and separable participle teruggegeven. Borg here means a refundable deposit, not a person guaranteeing a debt. The singular auxiliary heeft agrees with zij meaning she.
variation: Zij heeft ons de borg terugbetaald.

dutch: Dit is mijn verantwoordelijkheid.
cue: You volunteer to take ownership of a task that falls within your role.
scenario: You volunteer to take ownership of a task that falls within your role.
grammar: Dit is first and is second; mijn verantwoordelijkheid identifies the duty being pointed to. Verantwoordelijkheid is a de-word, but independent dit does not need to agree with it. Mijn is possessive. The noun refers to responsibility for a duty, rather than blame for a specific mistake in this scenario.
variation: Dat is mijn verantwoordelijkheid.

dutch: Ik zal het rapport versturen.
cue: You commit to sending the finished report after its final review.
scenario: You commit to sending the finished report after its final review.
grammar: Ik is first and zal second; the object stands before final versturen. Versturen is inseparable because of ver-; the infinitive remains whole. Rapport is a het-word. Zal expresses the speaker’s future commitment; its plural counterpart is zullen.
variation: Ik zal het rapport vanavond versturen.

dutch: Hoe betrouwbaar is deze meting?
cue: You compare repeated measurements and ask how much confidence you can place in the result.
scenario: You compare repeated measurements and ask how much confidence you can place in the result.
grammar: Hoe betrouwbaar is one question constituent, so is is second even though two words precede it. Deze meting is the subject. Betrouwbaar is predicative without -e. Meting is a de-word, so use deze. Hoe asks about the degree of reliability. A measurement’s reliability differs from whether a person is honest.
variation: Hoe betrouwbaar zijn deze metingen?

dutch: Positief blijven is belangrijk.
cue: After a setback, a colleague encourages the team to maintain a hopeful attitude.
scenario: After a setback, a colleague encourages the team to maintain a hopeful attitude.
grammar: Positief blijven is the first constituent and activity subject; is is second and belangrijk describes that activity. Blijven with an adjective means remain in a state. Positief remains uninflected as a predicative complement inside the subject phrase. The activity subject takes singular is.
variation: Rustig blijven is belangrijk.

dutch: Ben je bezig met de voorbereiding?
english: Are you busy with the preparation?
cue: You check whether a colleague is currently working on preparing an upcoming activity.
scenario: You check whether a colleague is currently working on preparing an upcoming activity.
grammar: Ben starts the yes/no question, followed by subject je, bezig, and the activity with met. Ben je is the inverted informal form of zijn. Bezig zijn met names an activity in progress. Voorbereiding is a de-word. Bezig is predicative and takes no -e.
variation: Ben je bezig met de uitnodigingen?

dutch: Hij legde zijn theorie uit.
cue: A colleague explains the reasoning behind a theory using a diagram and model.
scenario: A colleague explains the reasoning behind a theory using a diagram and model.
grammar: Hij is first and legde second. The object stands between legde and the final separable particle uit. Uitleggen is separable: legt uit; its singular past is legde uit. The doubled g in leggen reduces to one g before -de. Zijn is possessive before theorie.
variation: Zij legde haar theorie uit.

dutch: Controleer alstublieft mijn werk.
cue: You ask an experienced colleague to inspect the work you have completed.
scenario: You ask an experienced colleague to inspect the work you have completed.
grammar: Controleer begins the instruction/request, followed by alstublieft and the object mijn werk. Controleren has stem controleer. Alstublieft adds polite tone; it does not require a subject pronoun in an ordinary imperative. Mijn replaces the article before werk.
variation: Controleer alstublieft mijn berekening.

dutch: Praat nu, want straks begint de vergadering.
english: Talk now, because the meeting starts shortly.
cue: A colleague has a brief window to speak before a meeting begins.
scenario: A colleague has a brief window to speak before a meeting begins.
grammar: Praat nu is an imperative clause. After coordinating want, the second clause keeps main-clause order: straks first, begint second, then de vergadering. Want gives a reason without introducing subordinate verb-final order. Beginnen has singular begint. Straks means shortly/later soon, in contrast with nu.
variation: Praat nu, want straks is er geen tijd.

dutch: Wat is zijn volgende zet?
cue: You discuss a colleague’s next strategic action while planning the response to a business proposal.
scenario: You discuss a colleague’s next strategic action while planning the response to a business proposal.
grammar: Wat asks which action is next; is is second and zijn volgende zet follows as the subject. Zet means a strategic move in this context, not a seat or the verb put. De zet takes attributive volgende after possessive zijn. Zijn is possessive.
variation: Wat is hun volgende zet?

dutch: Hoe laat komt hij aan?
cue: You coordinate collecting a colleague from the station and ask for his arrival time.
scenario: You coordinate collecting a colleague from the station and ask for his arrival time.
grammar: Hoe laat is one question phrase; komt is second, followed by hij and final aan. Aankomen is separable: komt aan. The present can refer to a planned arrival. Komt retains -t with subject hij after it; the informal jij inversion exception does not apply to hij.
variation: Hoe laat komen zij aan?

dutch: We moeten competitief blijven.
cue: Your team discusses maintaining the quality and efficiency needed to compete with similar businesses.
scenario: Your team discusses maintaining the quality and efficiency needed to compete with similar businesses.
grammar: We is first and moeten second; competitief describes the state to maintain, and blijven is final. Moeten expresses necessity, not a suggestion with should. Blijven plus an adjective means remain in a state. Competitief is predicative and does not receive -e. After moeten use blijven without te.
variation: We moeten flexibel blijven.

dutch: Ik stuur een uitnodiging aan alle buren.
english: I'll send an invitation to all the neighbours.
cue: You organise a neighbourhood gathering and invite everyone living nearby.
scenario: You organise a neighbourhood gathering and invite everyone living nearby.
grammar: Ik is first and stuur second; the object precedes the recipient aan alle buren. The present stuur can express an immediate intention. Alle is a plural determiner before buren and does not combine with een. Aan marks the recipients. Uitnodiging is an indefinite singular de-word.
variation: We sturen een uitnodiging aan alle buren.

dutch: Ze oefenen geduld.
cue: Several people wait calmly for their turn at a service counter.
scenario: Several people wait calmly for their turn at a service counter.
grammar: Ze is first and oefenen second; geduld completes the fixed expression. Geduld oefenen is an established expression meaning to be patient, often while waiting. Geduld is uncountable and has no article here. Plural oefenen makes ze mean they. It need not mean a deliberate training exercise.
variation: We moeten geduld oefenen.

dutch: Hij zal hem de omleiding uitleggen.
english: He'll explain the diversion to him.
cue: A colleague will explain a changed road route to someone travelling to the office.
scenario: A colleague will explain a changed road route to someone travelling to the office.
grammar: Hij is first and zal second; short recipient hem comes before the full object, followed by uitleggen. Uitleggen is separable in a finite simple clause but stays whole as an infinitive after zal. Hem names the listener and is an object form. Omleiding means the rerouted road route in this context.
variation: Zij zal hem de omleiding uitleggen.

dutch: Wacht op hem bij de ingang.
english: Wait for him by the entrance.
cue: You ask a colleague to meet a late arrival at the entrance before entering together.
scenario: You ask a colleague to meet a late arrival at the entrance before entering together.
grammar: Wacht starts the instruction; op hem names the person expected, and bij de ingang locates the waiting. Wachten op is a fixed combination. Hem is an object pronoun after op. Bij marks a nearby location. Ingang is a de-word. This imperative uses the stem wacht.
variation: Wacht op haar bij de ingang.

dutch: Ik beloof je dat ik op tijd zal zijn.
english: I promise you that I'll be on time.
cue: You reassure a colleague that you will arrive punctually for an agreed meeting.
scenario: You reassure a colleague that you will arrive punctually for an agreed meeting.
grammar: Ik is first and beloof second; recipient je precedes the content clause. Its final verb group is zal zijn. Beloven can take a recipient and a dat-clause naming the promise. Je is an object pronoun. Op tijd means on time. In the subordinate future group, zal zijn is standard; zijn zal is also possible.
variation: Ik beloof je dat ik morgen zal komen.

dutch: Ik zie je morgen bij de halte.
english: I'll see you tomorrow at the stop.
cue: You arrange to meet a colleague by the bus stop the following day.
scenario: You arrange to meet a colleague by the bus stop the following day.
grammar: Ik is first and zie second; je is followed by the planned time and meeting place. Zien has the irregular ik form zie. Je is an object pronoun here. The future time morgen makes the present express a planned meeting. Halte is a de-word; bij means by/near.
variation: Ik zie je morgen bij het station.

dutch: Draag alstublieft de mappen voor mij.
english: Please carry the folders for me.
cue: With your hands occupied, you politely ask a colleague to carry a stack of folders.
scenario: With your hands occupied, you politely ask a colleague to carry a stack of folders.
grammar: Draag starts the imperative; alstublieft softens it. The object precedes the beneficiary voor mij. Dragen has stem draag and irregular participle gedragen. Mappen is the plural of de map, with doubled p preserving the short vowel. Mij is the stressed object pronoun after voor.
variation: Draag alstublieft de dozen voor mij.

dutch: Ik ben hier om aan het renovatieproject te werken.
english: I'm here to work on the renovation project.
cue: You arrive at a renovation site and explain the purpose of your visit.
scenario: You arrive at a renovation site and explain the purpose of your visit.
grammar: Ik is first and ben second; the purpose phrase follows hier and ends with te werken. Om ... te gives the purpose. Werken aan introduces the project being worked on. Renovatieproject is one compound and takes het from project. The project phrase precedes te werken.
variation: We zijn hier om aan het renovatieproject te werken.

dutch: Start dit programma na de installatie.
cue: A colleague asks you to open newly installed software once installation has finished.
scenario: A colleague asks you to open newly installed software once installation has finished.
grammar: Start begins the instruction, followed by its object and a time prepositional phrase. Programma is a het-word, so attributive this is dit. Start is the imperative stem. Na here means after, not the separable particle of nadenken. Installatie is a de-word.
variation: Start het programma na de installatie.

dutch: Ze richten zich op hun werk.
cue: Colleagues put distractions aside and concentrate on their assigned work.
scenario: Colleagues put distractions aside and concentrate on their assigned work.
grammar: Ze is first and richten second; reflexive zich comes before op hun werk. Zich richten op means focus on. The reflexive matches plural ze; with ik it is me. Hun is possessive before werk. Op belongs to the fixed expression.
variation: We richten ons op ons werk.

dutch: Hij vertrok vroeg omdat de trein uitviel.
english: He left early because the train was cancelled.
cue: A colleague leaves earlier than planned to arrange alternative transport after his train is cancelled.
scenario: A colleague leaves earlier than planned to arrange alternative transport after his train is cancelled.
grammar: Hij is first and vertrok second. In the omdat-clause, subject de trein precedes final uitviel. Vertrok is irregular singular past of vertrekken. Omdat introduces a subordinate reason clause. Uitvallen is separable, but in this verb-final subordinate clause its finite past uitviel stays together. A train uitvallen means not running/cancelled.
variation: Hij vertrok vroeg omdat de bus uitviel.

dutch: Wat is de beste aanpak?
cue: Your team compares ways to tackle a newly identified problem.
scenario: Your team compares ways to tackle a newly identified problem.
grammar: Wat asks for the chosen method; is is second and the subject follows. Aanpak is a de-word. Beste is the irregular superlative of goed and takes the attributive -e ending. De beste aanpak identifies the most suitable method among alternatives.
variation: Wat is de beste aanpak voor dit probleem?

dutch: Ik ga de kapotte rits repareren.
english: I'm going to repair the broken zip.
cue: You show a broken coat zip and state your intention to repair it.
scenario: You show a broken coat zip and state your intention to repair it.
grammar: Ik is first and ga second; the object stands before final repareren. Gaan + infinitive here states an intention, without requiring physical travel. Repareren takes no te after ga. Rits is a de-word, so the attributive adjective is kapotte.
variation: We gaan de kapotte rits repareren.

dutch: Laten we onze voortgang bekijken.
cue: Your team checks how much of a shared project has been completed.
scenario: Your team checks how much of a shared project has been completed.
grammar: Laten we introduces a shared suggestion; the object comes before final bekijken. Voortgang is a de-word, so our is onze. Bekijken is inseparable because of be- and stays whole. It means examine/review here, rather than simply look casually.
variation: Laten we onze voortgang samen bekijken.

dutch: Is dit jouw beslissing?
cue: You ask a colleague whether they personally made a choice rather than following someone else’s decision.
scenario: You ask a colleague whether they personally made a choice rather than following someone else’s decision.
grammar: Is begins the yes/no question; independent dit is the subject and jouw beslissing identifies the choice. Jouw is a stressed possessive, appropriate when contrasting whose decision it is. Jou would be an object pronoun. Beslissing is a de-word, but independent dit need not agree with it.
variation: Is dit jullie beslissing?

dutch: Hij is bezig met het controleren van de tijd.
cue: A colleague checks the clock while coordinating the timing of an activity.
scenario: A colleague checks the clock while coordinating the timing of an activity.
grammar: Hij is first and is second; bezig met is followed by a nominalised activity phrase. Het controleren is an infinitive used as a noun. Van de tijd names what is checked in the nominal construction; ordinary verb form would be de tijd controleren. Bezig met presents current involvement.
variation: Hij is bezig met het controleren van de planning.

dutch: Ik vond je idee leuk.
cue: You recall a creative suggestion from a colleague and tell them you liked it.
scenario: You recall a creative suggestion from a colleague and tell them you liked it.
grammar: Ik is first and vond second; je idee is the object and leuk evaluates it. Vinden in this construction means consider/find something nice. Vond is irregular singular past. Je is possessive. Leuk is an object predicate with no -e; it does not stand attributively before idee.
variation: We vonden je idee leuk.

dutch: Bevestig alstublieft uw boeking.
cue: A receptionist asks a guest to confirm a reservation before arrangements are finalised.
scenario: A receptionist asks a guest to confirm a reservation before arrangements are finalised.
grammar: Bevestig begins the request, followed by alstublieft and uw boeking. Bevestigen has stem bevestig. Uw is polite possessive. Boeking is a de-word meaning a reservation; it is not the noun boek meaning book. The prefix be- is inseparable.
variation: Bevestig alstublieft uw reservering.

dutch: We denken na over het risico van deze investering.
english: We're considering the risk of this investment.
cue: Your team reviews the uncertainty of an investment proposal before deciding.
scenario: Your team reviews the uncertainty of an investment proposal before deciding.
grammar: We is first and denken second; na is separated from the verb, followed by the full topic phrase. Nadenken over means reflect on. Risico is a het-word; investering is a de-word and takes deze. Van specifies which risk is considered.
variation: We denken na over de gevolgen van deze investering.

dutch: Wat is ons concurrentievoordeel ten opzichte van grotere bedrijven?
english: What's our competitive advantage compared with larger companies?
cue: A small team compares its particular strengths with those of larger competitors.
scenario: A small team compares its particular strengths with those of larger competitors.
grammar: Wat is first and is second; the subject is followed by a comparison phrase naming the competitors. Concurrentievoordeel is one compound with het voordeel as its head, so possessive our is ons. Ten opzichte van means relative to/compared with. Grotere is an attributive comparative before plural bedrijven.
variation: Wat is ons voordeel ten opzichte van grotere bedrijven?

dutch: Zal deze oplossing werken?
cue: You ask whether a proposed arrangement will solve an access problem before testing it.
scenario: You ask whether a proposed arrangement will solve an access problem before testing it.
grammar: Zal starts the yes/no question, followed by its subject and final infinitive werken. Werken here means function or succeed, not perform a job. Oplossing is a de-word and takes deze. The singular subject requires zal. Zullen asks about a predicted result.
variation: Zal dit plan werken?

dutch: We hebben onze manager nodig om dit conflict op te lossen.
english: We need our manager to resolve this conflict.
cue: Your team asks a manager to help resolve a disagreement between colleagues.
scenario: Your team asks a manager to help resolve a disagreement between colleagues.
grammar: We is first and hebben second. The need expression ends with nodig, followed by the purpose clause. Manager is a de-word, so possessive our is onze. Conflict is a het-word and takes dit. Oplossen is separable; te goes between op and lossen in the purpose infinitive.
variation: We hebben hulp nodig om dit conflict op te lossen.

dutch: Laten we ons succes vieren.
cue: After reaching a shared goal, you invite the team to a small celebration.
scenario: After reaching a shared goal, you invite the team to a small celebration.
grammar: Laten we introduces the shared proposal; ons succes precedes final vieren. Succes is a singular het-word, so our is ons. Vieren is an infinitive after Laten we. The proposal includes the speaker and colleagues in celebrating a completed success.
variation: Laten we ons succes samen vieren.

dutch: Dit is erg belangrijk voor onze samenwerking.
english: This is very important for our cooperation.
cue: You stress the importance of an agreed way to share information during a joint project.
scenario: You stress the importance of an agreed way to share information during a joint project.
grammar: Dit is first and is second. Erg modifies belangrijk; voor introduces what the importance concerns. Dit stands independently. Erg is a degree adverb, not an attributive adjective here. Samenwerking is a de-word and takes onze. Belangrijk is predicative without -e.
variation: Dit is erg belangrijk voor ons project.

dutch: Leg ons het verschil tussen deze materialen uit.
english: Explain the difference between these materials to us.
cue: You ask a specialist to explain how two material samples differ.
scenario: You ask a specialist to explain how two material samples differ.
grammar: Leg starts the instruction and uit ends it; recipient ons and the full object stand inside that bracket. Uitleggen is separable, with imperative leg ... uit. Verschil is a het-word; tussen names the compared items. Deze agrees with plural materialen. A short recipient naturally precedes a full noun object.
variation: Leg ons het verschil tussen deze kleuren uit.

dutch: Heb je mijn fiets voor me gerepareerd?
english: Have you repaired my bicycle for me?
cue: You collect your bicycle and ask whether a colleague has completed the repair for you.
scenario: You collect your bicycle and ask whether a colleague has completed the repair for you.
grammar: Heb starts the perfect question, then je, the object and beneficiary, followed by gerepareerd. Heb je is inverted and lacks -t with subject je. Repareren uses hebben and participle gerepareerd. Mijn is possessive; me after voor is an object beneficiary pronoun.
variation: Heb je mijn fiets voor mij gerepareerd?

dutch: Zal de reparatie lang duren?
english: Will the repair take a long time?
cue: You ask how much time a repair is likely to require before deciding whether to wait.
scenario: You ask how much time a repair is likely to require before deciding whether to wait.
grammar: Zal starts the question, followed by its subject, lang, and final infinitive duren. Duren concerns how long an event takes or lasts. Lang makes the intended duration question explicit; it does not assess whether a repaired object is durable. Reparatie is a singular de-word.
variation: Zal de installatie lang duren?

dutch: De klant heeft het definitieve ontwerp goedgekeurd.
english: The customer has approved the final design.
cue: A customer signs off the final version of a design before production begins.
scenario: A customer signs off the final version of a design before production begins.
grammar: De klant is first and heeft second; the object precedes final goedgekeurd. Goedkeuren is separable: keurt goed; its participle is goedgekeurd. Ontwerp is a het-word, but after definite het the adjective receives -e: definitieve. The perfect presents completed approval.
variation: De klant heeft het nieuwe ontwerp goedgekeurd.

dutch: Hij maakte het werk af.
cue: A colleague completes the remaining work on a task and clears away his tools.
scenario: A colleague completes the remaining work on a task and clears away his tools.
grammar: Hij is first and maakte second; the object stands before final particle af. Afmaken is separable. Its singular past is maakte af; the participle is afgemaakt. Werk is a het-word and is the object of finishing. This simple past differs from heeft afgemaakt.
variation: Zij maakte het werk af.

dutch: Je hebt geen fout gemaakt.
cue: You reassure a colleague after checking that their work is correct.
scenario: You reassure a colleague after checking that their work is correct.
grammar: Je is first and hebt second; geen fout precedes final gemaakt. Geen negates indefinite een fout: no mistake/not a mistake. Hebt gemaakt is a perfect; maken uses hebben. Je before the verb requires hebt with -t.
variation: Je hebt geen fouten gemaakt.

dutch: Bel haar na de lunch.
cue: You ask a colleague to telephone a contact after the lunch break.
scenario: You ask a colleague to telephone a contact after the lunch break.
grammar: Bel begins the instruction; haar is the person called and na de lunch gives the time. Bellen directly takes a person as object. Haar is an object pronoun here, not possessive. Bel is the imperative stem, with one l; na means after.
variation: Bel haar na de vergadering.

dutch: Zijn vergadering begint spoedig.
cue: You warn a colleague that the meeting he is due to attend is about to begin.
scenario: You warn a colleague that the meeting he is due to attend is about to begin.
grammar: Zijn vergadering is first and begint second; spoedig gives the approaching time. Zijn is possessive, not a verb. Vergadering is singular, requiring begint. Spoedig means soon and has a relatively formal tone; binnenkort or straks can fit different time frames.
variation: Zijn vergadering begint straks.

dutch: Wie belt er?
cue: You hear an incoming call and ask which person is calling.
scenario: You hear an incoming call and ask which person is calling.
grammar: Wie is the question subject, followed by belt and presentative er; no additional subject pronoun is needed. Wie normally takes singular agreement in this unspecified question. Er is common in presentative subject questions and need not be translated as a literal place. Belt can mean telephones here.
variation: Wie belt er nu?

dutch: Wat zijn de belangrijkste inzichten?
cue: After a workshop, you ask the group to identify the most important things they learned.
scenario: After a workshop, you ask the group to identify the most important things they learned.
grammar: Wat asks for the content, zijn is second, and the plural subject follows. Inzichten is plural, so the verb is zijn. Belangrijkste is the attributive superlative of belangrijk. Inzicht means understanding or insight, not a physical view in this context.
variation: Wat zijn de belangrijkste conclusies?

dutch: Wat is de datum van de inschrijving?
cue: You ask when registration for a course takes place.
scenario: You ask when registration for a course takes place.
grammar: Wat is first and is second; the full date phrase is the subject. Datum is a de-word. Van de inschrijving specifies which date is requested, rather than asking for today’s date. Inschrijving means registration in this context.
variation: Wat is de datum van de bijeenkomst?

dutch: Heb je me de factuur gestuurd?
english: Have you sent me the invoice?
cue: You ask whether the invoice needed for payment has already been sent to you.
scenario: You ask whether the invoice needed for payment has already been sent to you.
grammar: Heb starts the perfect question; subject je, recipient me and the full object come before gestuurd. Sturen uses hebben and participle gestuurd. Heb je loses -t with the following informal subject. Factuur is a de-word. A short indirect object naturally precedes a full direct object.
variation: Heb je me de rekening gestuurd?

dutch: Ik wil de beschadigde stoel repareren.
english: I want to repair the damaged chair.
cue: You want to repair a damaged chair rather than discard it.
scenario: You want to repair a damaged chair rather than discard it.
grammar: Ik is first and wil second; the damaged chair stands before final repareren. Willen means want, not the English future will. Repareren takes no te after wil. Beschadigde is an attributive participle/adjective before de stoel.
variation: We willen de beschadigde stoel repareren.

dutch: Zij delen hun ideeën.
cue: Team members contribute different ideas and discuss them openly.
scenario: Team members contribute different ideas and discuss them openly.
grammar: Zij is first and delen second; hun ideeën is the object. Plural delen makes zij mean they. Hun is possessive before ideeën. Idee has plural ideeën with a diaeresis to show the vowel begins a new syllable.
variation: We delen onze ideeën.

dutch: Kunt u me erdoorheen leiden?
english: Could you guide me through it?
cue: You politely ask a colleague to guide you step by step through an unfamiliar procedure.
scenario: You politely ask a colleague to guide you step by step through an unfamiliar procedure.
grammar: Kunt starts the request, followed by u and me; erdoorheen specifies the process and leiden is final. Leiden means guide/lead, not lijden meaning suffer. Erdoorheen refers back to the procedure: through it. Kunt u is standard; kan u is also standard. The infinitive follows the modal without te.
variation: Kunt u me door de procedure leiden?

dutch: Heeft u zijn werk beoordeeld?
cue: You politely ask a supervisor whether they have evaluated a colleague’s finished work.
scenario: You politely ask a supervisor whether they have evaluated a colleague’s finished work.
grammar: Heeft starts the perfect question, followed by polite subject u, object and final beoordeeld. Heeft u and hebt u are both standard. Beoordelen is inseparable with participle beoordeeld, without added ge-. Zijn is possessive; werk is the object rather than the subject.
variation: Hebt u zijn werk beoordeeld?

dutch: Bedankt voor uw geduld tijdens het wachten.
english: Thank you for your patience while waiting.
cue: After a delay at a reception desk, you thank a guest for waiting patiently.
scenario: After a delay at a reception desk, you thank a guest for waiting patiently.
grammar: Bedankt begins a conventional thanks expression without a finite verb; the following phrases name the reason and time. Bedankt voor is a standard polite expression. Uw is possessive. Geduld is uncountable; het wachten is a nominalised infinitive after tijdens. It is natural standalone thanks, not a finite full clause.
variation: Bedankt voor uw geduld.

dutch: Koop de treinkaart voor hem.
english: Buy the train ticket for him.
cue: You ask a colleague to buy a train ticket on behalf of someone who cannot do it themselves.
scenario: You ask a colleague to buy a train ticket on behalf of someone who cannot do it themselves.
grammar: Koop starts the instruction; the object comes before beneficiary voor hem. Kopen has stem koop. Voor names the person benefiting from the purchase. Hem is an object form after the preposition. Treinkaart is a compound with de kaart as its head.
variation: Koop de treinkaart voor haar.

dutch: Ze heeft mijn idee gestolen.
cue: You object when another person presents your original concept as her own.
scenario: You object when another person presents your original concept as her own.
grammar: Ze is first and heeft second; mijn idee stands before final gestolen. Stelen has irregular participle gestolen and uses hebben. Singular heeft makes ze mean she. Mijn is possessive. Een idee stelen is figurative taking credit for someone else’s idea.
variation: Hij heeft mijn idee gestolen.

dutch: Hij werkte heel hard.
cue: You recall the sustained effort a colleague put into a demanding task.
scenario: You recall the sustained effort a colleague put into a demanding task.
grammar: Hij is first and werkte second; heel modifies manner adverb hard. Werken has singular past werkte with -te. Hard describes effort rather than the physical hardness of an object. Heel means very and modifies hard; both are adverbial here.
variation: Zij werkte heel hard.

dutch: Je zag er erg vermoeid uit.
cue: You notice that a colleague looked exhausted after a long workday.
scenario: You notice that a colleague looked exhausted after a long workday.
grammar: Je is first and zag second; er and uit surround the appearance description. Er ... uitzien describes appearance. Zag is irregular past of zien; uit separates in a main clause. Er belongs to the appearance construction and is not a literal place. Vermoeid is predicative without -e.
variation: Je zag er erg moe uit.

dutch: Breng de monsters naar het laboratorium.
english: Take the samples to the laboratory.
cue: You ask a colleague to deliver test samples to a laboratory.
scenario: You ask a colleague to deliver test samples to a laboratory.
grammar: Breng starts the instruction; the object precedes the destination naar het laboratorium. Brengen has stem breng and irregular participle gebracht. Monsters means test samples here, not mythical creatures. Laboratorium is a het-word. Naar marks the destination.
variation: Breng de monsters naar de onderzoeker.

dutch: Wat is het algemene doel van deze opleiding?
english: What's the overall aim of this training course?
cue: At the start of a training course, you ask what the course as a whole is intended to achieve.
scenario: At the start of a training course, you ask what the course as a whole is intended to achieve.
grammar: Wat asks for the aim; is is second and the complete subject phrase follows. Doel is a het-word, but definite het requires attributive algemene with -e. Opleiding is a de-word and takes deze. Van specifies the course whose aim is asked about.
variation: Wat is het algemene doel van dit project?

dutch: Hoeveel tijd hebben we?
english: How much time do we have?
cue: You ask how much time remains to finish an activity before the next appointment.
scenario: You ask how much time remains to finish an activity before the next appointment.
grammar: Hoeveel tijd is the first question constituent and object; hebben is second and subject we follows. Tijd is uncountable in this quantity use. Hoeveel asks for an amount; many countable hours would be hoeveel uur. Plural subject we requires hebben.
variation: Hoeveel tijd hebben jullie?

dutch: Mag ik mijn laptop gebruiken?
cue: You ask permission to use your laptop during a training session.
scenario: You ask permission to use your laptop during a training session.
grammar: Mag starts the permission question; ik and the object follow, and gebruiken is final. Mogen expresses permission, whereas kunnen primarily expresses ability or possibility. Mijn is possessive. Gebruiken after mag takes no te. Mag is singular present of mogen.
variation: Mag ik mijn telefoon gebruiken?

dutch: Haar computer is offline.
cue: A colleague’s computer is disconnected from the network during a work session.
scenario: A colleague’s computer is disconnected from the network during a work session.
grammar: Haar computer is the first constituent; is is second and offline describes its connection state. Haar is possessive, not an object pronoun here. Computer is singular, requiring is. Offline means not connected to the network; it does not necessarily mean the machine is broken.
variation: Zijn computer is offline.

dutch: Dit werkblad is gemakkelijk schoon te maken.
english: This worktop is easy to clean.
cue: You show a smooth work surface that can be wiped clean with little effort.
scenario: You show a smooth work surface that can be wiped clean with little effort.
grammar: Dit werkblad is first and is second; gemakkelijk is followed by the final infinitive phrase schoon te maken. Werkblad is a het-word, so use dit. Schoonmaken is separable, with te between schoon and maken. Gemakkelijk is predicative without -e. The worktop is what gets cleaned.
variation: Deze tafel is gemakkelijk schoon te maken.

dutch: Dit is onze agenda voor de studiedag.
english: This is our agenda for the training day.
cue: You show the planned list of sessions and discussion items for a shared training day.
scenario: You show the planned list of sessions and discussion items for a shared training day.
grammar: Independent Dit is first and is second; the following noun phrase identifies the schedule of activities. Agenda here means the planned list of items/sessions, not a personal appointment diary. It is a de-word and takes onze. Dit stands independently and need not agree with agenda. Studiedag is a compound ending in de dag.
variation: Dit is onze agenda voor de bijeenkomst.

dutch: We werkten op kantoor.
cue: You recall working together at the office rather than remotely.
scenario: You recall working together at the office rather than remotely.
grammar: We is first and werkten second; op kantoor gives the workplace. Werkten is plural simple past of werken, with -ten. Op kantoor is a conventional workplace expression without an article. It does not mean physically standing on top of an office.
variation: We werkten thuis.

dutch: Ik begrijp waarom je twijfelt.
english: I understand why you are unsure.
cue: You listen to a colleague’s concerns and acknowledge why they hesitate.
scenario: You listen to a colleague’s concerns and acknowledge why they hesitate.
grammar: Ik is first and begrijp second; the embedded why-clause is its object, with twijfelt final. Begrijpen is inseparable because of be-. Waarom introduces an embedded question, not a direct question with inversion. Je before its finite verb requires twijfelt with -t. Twijfelen means doubt or hesitate.
variation: Ik begrijp waarom je aarzelt.

dutch: Dit fietspad is erg veilig.
english: This cycle path is very safe.
cue: You describe a protected cycle path separated from road traffic.
scenario: You describe a protected cycle path separated from road traffic.
grammar: Dit fietspad is first and is second; erg modifies veilig. Fietspad is a het-word, so this is dit before the noun. Veilig is predicative without -e. Erg means very as a degree adverb.
variation: Dit pad is erg veilig.

dutch: Is dit uw verslag van het ongeval?
english: Is this your report of the accident?
cue: A receptionist checks which guest wrote a submitted accident report.
scenario: A receptionist checks which guest wrote a submitted accident report.
grammar: Is starts the question; independent dit is subject and the report phrase follows it. Uw is polite possessive; u is a personal pronoun. Verslag and ongeval are het-words. Van specifies the event described. Independent dit is not an attributive demonstrative of verslag.
variation: Is dat uw verslag van het bezoek?

dutch: Hij verkoopt zijn fiets aan hen.
english: He sells his bicycle to them.
cue: A colleague sells his bicycle to two interested neighbours.
scenario: A colleague sells his bicycle to two interested neighbours.
grammar: Hij is first and verkoopt second; the sold item precedes recipient aan hen. Verkopen is inseparable and takes third-person verkoopt. Hen is the standard stressed plural object form after a preposition; unstressed ze is also possible. Zijn is possessive before fiets.
variation: Hij verkoopt zijn fiets aan ze.

dutch: Wat is je plan voor de verhuizing?
english: What's your plan for the move?
cue: You ask how a colleague intends to organise moving to a new home.
scenario: You ask how a colleague intends to organise moving to a new home.
grammar: Wat is first and is second; the plan phrase is the subject. Je is possessive before plan, not the subject of is. Plan is a het-word. Voor specifies the move the plan concerns. Verhuizing is a de-word.
variation: Wat is jullie plan voor de verhuizing?

dutch: Kunt u mij het rapport sturen?
english: Could you send me the report?
cue: You politely ask a colleague to send you a finished report for review.
scenario: You politely ask a colleague to send you a finished report for review.
grammar: Kunt starts the request; u, recipient mij and the object come before final sturen. Kunt u and kan u are both standard. Mij is a stressed recipient object, with me possible unstressed. Sturen after a modal is an infinitive without te. Rapport is a het-word.
variation: Kunt u me het rapport sturen?

dutch: Wat is hun grootste obstakel bij het vinden van huisvesting?
english: What's their biggest obstacle to finding accommodation?
cue: You discuss why a group is having difficulty finding suitable accommodation.
scenario: You discuss why a group is having difficulty finding suitable accommodation.
grammar: Wat is first and is second; the whole obstacle phrase is subject. Hun is possessive. Grootste is an attributive superlative. Het vinden is a nominalised infinitive after bij; van huisvesting names what is being found. Huisvesting is uncountable accommodation.
variation: Wat is hun grootste probleem bij het vinden van huisvesting?

dutch: Mag ik je pen lenen om dit formulier te ondertekenen?
english: May I borrow your pen to sign this form?
cue: At a reception desk, you ask to borrow a pen so you can sign a form.
scenario: At a reception desk, you ask to borrow a pen so you can sign a form.
grammar: Mag starts the permission question, then ik, je pen and lenen. The following purpose phrase ends with te ondertekenen. Mogen expresses permission. Je is possessive before pen. Lenen means borrow from the owner in this context. Ondertekenen is inseparable, so te goes before the whole infinitive. Formulier is a het-word and takes dit.
variation: Mag ik uw pen lenen om dit formulier te ondertekenen?

dutch: Ik ben te laat voor de laatste tram.
english: I'm too late for the last tram.
cue: You reach a tram stop after the last tram has already left.
scenario: You reach a tram stop after the last tram has already left.
grammar: Ik is first and ben second; te laat is followed by the missed event with voor. Te before laat is a degree word, not an infinitive marker. Tram is a de-word; laatste is attributive with -e. Ben is the ik form of zijn.
variation: We zijn te laat voor de laatste tram.

dutch: We moeten innovatie stimuleren.
cue: Your team discusses supporting new ideas and experiments in its work.
scenario: Your team discusses supporting new ideas and experiments in its work.
grammar: We is first and moeten second; innovatie precedes final stimuleren. Moeten expresses necessity. Innovatie is an abstract uncountable noun without an article here. Stimuleren is an infinitive without te after moeten.
variation: We moeten creativiteit stimuleren.

dutch: Wat is hun geheime wapen bij het bakken van brood?
english: What's their secret weapon for baking bread?
cue: You ask skilled bakers what special technique gives their bread its distinctive quality.
scenario: You ask skilled bakers what special technique gives their bread its distinctive quality.
grammar: Wat is first and is second; the full figurative weapon phrase is subject. Geheime wapen is figurative for a special strength or technique. Hun is possessive. Het bakken is a nominalised infinitive after bij; van brood names what is baked. No physical weapon is meant.
variation: Wat is hun geheim bij het bakken van brood?

dutch: Het spijt me, de koffieautomaat is kapot.
english: I'm sorry, the coffee machine is broken.
cue: You apologise to a visitor because the coffee machine is unavailable due to a fault.
scenario: You apologise to a visitor because the coffee machine is unavailable due to a fault.
grammar: Two short main clauses are linked by a comma in this spoken-style apology. Each has its own subject and finite verb. Het spijt me is an idiomatic apology; me is the experiencer object. Koffieautomaat is a de-word. Kapot is predicative without -e. The machine being broken does not itself say who caused the damage.
variation: Het spijt me, de printer is kapot.

dutch: Wat is het volgende getal in deze reeks?
english: What's the next number in this sequence?
cue: During an exercise, you ask a learner to identify the next number in a sequence.
scenario: During an exercise, you ask a learner to identify the next number in a sequence.
grammar: Wat is first and is second; the next-number phrase follows as subject. Getal is a het-word; definite het takes attributive volgende. Reeks is a de-word and takes deze. The noun makes the omitted next thing explicit in a number-pattern situation.
variation: Wat is het volgende woord in deze reeks?

dutch: Ik regel de logistiek.
cue: You volunteer to organise transport, delivery and materials for a shared activity.
scenario: You volunteer to organise transport, delivery and materials for a shared activity.
grammar: Ik is first and regel second; de logistiek is the direct object. Regelen has the ik form regel. Logistiek names practical organisation of movement and supplies and takes de. The present expresses a commitment in context, not necessarily an action already complete.
variation: We regelen de logistiek.

dutch: Wat is de volgende stap bij het aanvragen van een vergunning?
english: What's the next step in applying for a permit?
cue: At an administrative desk, you ask what to do next in the permit application process.
scenario: At an administrative desk, you ask what to do next in the permit application process.
grammar: Wat is first and is second; the full next-step phrase is subject. Stap is a de-word. Het aanvragen is a nominalised infinitive after bij; van een vergunning specifies what is requested. Aanvragen is separable in a finite clause, but stays whole in this activity noun.
variation: Wat is de volgende stap in deze aanvraag?

dutch: We kijken uit naar de start van de taalcursus.
english: We're looking forward to the start of the language course.
cue: You and fellow learners eagerly await a language course that has not begun yet.
scenario: You and fellow learners eagerly await a language course that has not begun yet.
grammar: We is first and kijken second; uit is separated and the anticipated event follows naar. Uitkijken naar means look forward to. This noun reference uses naar de start, unlike pronominal ernaar uitkijken. Taalcursus is a de-compound; van specifies what starts. The event is still in the future.
variation: We kijken uit naar het begin van de taalcursus.

dutch: Ik ben hier om de lift te repareren.
english: I'm here to repair the lift.
cue: A technician arrives at a building and explains the reason for the visit.
scenario: A technician arrives at a building and explains the reason for the visit.
grammar: Ik is first and ben second; the purpose phrase follows hier and ends with te repareren. Om ... te expresses purpose. Lift is a de-word; it is the object within the infinitive phrase. Repareren is not separable, so te stands before the whole verb.
variation: We zijn hier om de lift te repareren.

dutch: Dit formulier is snel in te vullen.
english: This form can be filled in quickly.
cue: You show a short form that requires only a few entries to complete.
scenario: You show a short form that requires only a few entries to complete.
grammar: Dit formulier is first and is second. Snel describes completing speed; in te vullen is the final infinitive phrase. Formulier is a het-word and takes dit. Invullen is separable, with te between in and vullen. The construction presents the form as something that can be completed quickly; snel is adverbial here.
variation: Deze kaart is snel in te vullen.

dutch: Ze zullen te laat zijn voor de inschrijving.
english: They'll be too late for registration.
cue: You expect two applicants to arrive after registration has finished.
scenario: You expect two applicants to arrive after registration has finished.
grammar: Ze is first and zullen second; te laat precedes infinitive zijn, followed by the registration phrase. Zullen agrees with plural ze. Zijn after the auxiliary is an infinitive. Te is a degree word before laat, not an infinitive marker. The sentence predicts future lateness.
variation: We zullen te laat zijn voor de inschrijving.

dutch: Ik was niet op kantoor toen de levering aankwam.
english: I wasn't at the office when the delivery arrived.
cue: You explain why you did not receive a delivery personally at the office.
scenario: You explain why you did not receive a delivery personally at the office.
grammar: Ik is first and was second. The toen-clause follows the location and ends with its finite verb aankwam. Toen refers to a particular past moment. Aankomen is separable, but finite aankwam stays whole in this subordinate clause. Op kantoor is a conventional article-free location expression.
variation: Ik was niet thuis toen de levering aankwam.

dutch: Het is beter om op de bevestiging te wachten.
english: It's better to wait for confirmation.
cue: You compare acting immediately with waiting until an arrangement has been confirmed.
scenario: You compare acting immediately with waiting until an arrangement has been confirmed.
grammar: Het is first and is second; beter evaluates the action named by the following infinitive phrase. Beter is comparative better, not superlative best. Het anticipates the action clause. Wachten op is fixed; om ... te names the evaluated action here rather than the purpose of a visit. Bevestiging is a de-word.
variation: Het is beter om op het antwoord te wachten.

dutch: Leg me alsjeblieft de inhoud van deze brief uit.
english: Please explain the content of this letter to me.
cue: You ask a colleague to explain a letter whose content you do not understand.
scenario: You ask a colleague to explain a letter whose content you do not understand.
grammar: Leg begins the instruction and uit ends it; recipient, politeness word and object stand between them. Uitleggen is separable. Inhoud is a de-word; deze agrees with de brief. Me is a recipient object. Alsjeblieft is the informal politeness word, compared with formal alstublieft.
variation: Leg me alsjeblieft deze brief uit.

dutch: Ik ben van plan in België te blijven wonen.
english: I'm planning to continue living in Belgium.
cue: You explain that you intend to keep living in Belgium rather than move abroad.
scenario: You explain that you intend to keep living in Belgium rather than move abroad.
grammar: Ik is first and ben second. The intended activity follows van plan and ends with te blijven wonen. Van plan zijn takes a te-infinitive, optionally introduced by om. Blijven wonen expresses continued residence; wonen follows blijven without another te. België uses a diaeresis. This is intention, not seeking an opportunity.
variation: Ik ben van plan om in België te blijven wonen.

dutch: Laten we over ideeën voor een buurtfeest brainstormen.
english: Let's brainstorm ideas for a neighbourhood party.
cue: Neighbours propose generating ideas together for a community gathering.
scenario: Neighbours propose generating ideas together for a community gathering.
grammar: Laten we introduces the shared proposal; the topic over ideas stands before final brainstormen. Brainstormen is commonly used with over for the topic. Ideeën is plural with a diaeresis. Buurtfeest is a compound ending in het feest, indefinite een here. The proposal infinitive has no te.
variation: Laten we over het buurtfeest brainstormen.

dutch: Het is belangrijk om kalm te blijven tijdens een conflict.
english: It's important to stay calm during a conflict.
cue: A colleague stresses remaining calm when discussing a disagreement.
scenario: A colleague stresses remaining calm when discussing a disagreement.
grammar: Het is first and is second; belangrijk evaluates the following action/state infinitive phrase. Het anticipates the clause describing what is important. Kalm is predicative after blijven and has no -e. Om ... te names the evaluated action; tijdens introduces the time circumstance.
variation: Het is belangrijk om rustig te blijven.

dutch: Deze parkeerautomaat is gemakkelijk te gebruiken.
english: This parking meter is easy to use.
cue: You show a visitor how straightforward the parking payment machine is to operate.
scenario: You show a visitor how straightforward the parking payment machine is to operate.
grammar: Deze parkeerautomaat is first and is second; gemakkelijk is followed by te gebruiken. Parkeerautomaat is a de-word and takes deze. Gemakkelijk is predicative without -e. The machine is the thing used in the te-infinitive construction, not the person doing the using.
variation: Deze automaat is gemakkelijk te gebruiken.

dutch: We moeten onze doelen op elkaar afstemmen.
english: We have to align our goals with each other.
cue: Two colleagues lay their separate plans side by side and agree on shared goals.
scenario: Two colleagues lay their separate plans side by side and agree on shared goals.
grammar: We is first and moeten second; the object and op elkaar come before final afstemmen. Afstemmen op means to coordinate with. Elkaar is reciprocal: the goals are aligned with each other. Onze agrees with plural doelen. After moeten the separable infinitive stays whole, without te.
variation: We stemmen onze doelen op elkaar af.

dutch: Hij voltooide zijn opleiding zonder financiële steun.
english: He completed his training without financial support.
cue: A colleague proudly holds his training certificate after paying for the course himself.
scenario: A colleague proudly holds his training certificate after paying for the course himself.
grammar: Hij is first and past-tense voltooide second; the object is followed by the without phrase. Voltooien has regular past voltooide. Zijn is possessive, not a finite verb. Financiële has -e before the de-word steun. Steun is uncountable here. Zonder introduces what was absent.
variation: Zij voltooide haar opleiding zonder financiële steun.

dutch: Ik ben bang voor mislukking.
cue: Before attempting an important new project, you admit your fear to a supportive colleague.
scenario: Before attempting an important new project, you admit your fear to a supportive colleague.
grammar: Ik is first and ben second; bang takes its fear object with voor. Bang voor is a fixed adjective-preposition combination. Bang is predicative without -e. Abstract mislukking can refer to failure generally without an article. A particular failed attempt would be een mislukking.
variation: We zijn bang voor mislukking.

dutch: Dit is mijn grootste uitdaging tijdens de stage.
english: This is my greatest challenge during the internship.
cue: An intern looks at a demanding assembly task while explaining why it is the hardest part of the placement.
scenario: An intern looks at a demanding assembly task while explaining why it is the hardest part of the placement.
grammar: Dit is first and is second; the challenge phrase is followed by the internship period. Grootste is the superlative of groot, used with -e before uitdaging. Mijn is possessive. Stage means internship or work placement, not an English performance stage. Tijdens takes a noun phrase.
variation: Dit is mijn moeilijkste taak tijdens de stage.

dutch: We moeten de verwarming aanzetten.
english: We have to turn on the heating.
cue: Two people in coats stand beside a cold radiator and reach for its control.
scenario: Two people in coats stand beside a cold radiator and reach for its control.
grammar: We is first and moeten second; the object comes before final aanzetten. Aanzetten is separable: We zetten de verwarming aan. After moeten it remains one infinitive without te. Verwarming is a de-word and here means the heating system.
variation: We zetten de verwarming aan.

dutch: Ik ben hier om te blijven.
cue: A new team member settles personal belongings on a desk and reassures a welcoming colleague of a lasting commitment.
scenario: A new team member settles personal belongings on a desk and reassures a welcoming colleague of a lasting commitment.
grammar: Ik is first and ben second; hier is followed by the om te phrase. Om te blijven expresses intention. Blijven is an infinitive after te. The idiom signals a lasting presence or commitment, rather than only remaining for a few minutes. Hier points to the current workplace.
variation: Wij zijn hier om te blijven.

dutch: We kijken uit naar het antwoord op onze sollicitatie.
english: We're looking forward to the reply to our job application.
cue: Two job applicants wait hopefully for a reply while looking at their submitted application materials.
scenario: Two job applicants wait hopefully for a reply while looking at their submitted application materials.
grammar: We is first and kijken second. The particle uit precedes the naar phrase naming the anticipated reply. Uitkijken naar means to look forward to. Antwoord op introduces what the reply concerns. Onze agrees with the de-word sollicitatie. This present sentence expresses anticipation, not receipt of the answer.
variation: Ik kijk uit naar het antwoord op mijn sollicitatie.

dutch: We zullen proberen het lek in het dak te repareren.
english: We'll try to repair the leak in the roof.
cue: Two people examine a leaking roof above a bucket and prepare tools to attempt the repair.
scenario: Two people examine a leaking roof above a bucket and prepare tools to attempt the repair.
grammar: Zullen is finite in second position, followed by proberen and its complement containing object plus te repareren. Zullen takes proberen without te; proberen takes te repareren. Lek and dak are het-words. The promise concerns an attempt; success is not guaranteed. In het dak specifies the location of the leak.
variation: We zullen het lek in het dak proberen te repareren.

dutch: Gelieve uw status bij te werken.
cue: An administrator politely asks a colleague at a shared project desk to update a task-status indicator.
scenario: An administrator politely asks a colleague at a shared project desk to update a task-status indicator.
grammar: The formal request begins with fixed Gelieve; uw status precedes the separable te-infinitive bij te werken. Gelieve in this fixed request formula is an old subjunctive form, with understood subject u; it is not the ordinary imperative stem. Uw is formal possessive. Bijwerken is separable, so te goes between bij and werken. This wording is formal and mainly written.
variation: Wilt u uw status bijwerken?

dutch: Vraag hem de weg naar het station.
english: Ask him for directions to the station.
cue: You direct a visitor with a travel bag to ask a nearby local person for the way to the station.
scenario: You direct a visitor with a travel bag to ask a nearby local person for the way to the station.
grammar: The imperative Vraag starts the instruction. The short recipient hem comes before the full object phrase. Iemand de weg vragen means to ask someone for directions. Hem is an object pronoun. Weg is a de-word; station is a het-word. Naar introduces the destination.
variation: Vraag haar de weg naar het station.

dutch: Wat zijn uw verwachtingen?
cue: A trainer invites a new participant to explain what they hope to gain from a course.
scenario: A trainer invites a new participant to explain what they hope to gain from a course.
grammar: Wat is first and zijn second; plural uw verwachtingen is the subject. Verwachtingen is plural, requiring zijn. Uw is formal possessive, not subject u. Wat asks for the content of the expectations. A singular question would be Wat is uw verwachting?
variation: Wat zijn je verwachtingen?

dutch: Zij is klaar om haar voorstel toe te lichten.
english: She's ready to explain her proposal.
cue: A prepared presenter waits beside her proposal materials, ready to explain them to a small group.
scenario: A prepared presenter waits beside her proposal materials, ready to explain them to a small group.
grammar: Zij is first and is second; klaar is followed by an om phrase with object and final toe te lichten. Klaar om expresses readiness for an action. Toelichten is separable, so its te-infinitive is toe te lichten. Haar is possessive with voorstel. Ready does not mean that the explanation has already begun.
variation: Hij is klaar om zijn voorstel toe te lichten.

dutch: Dit vereist onmiddellijke aandacht.
cue: A colleague points urgently to water leaking beside office equipment and asks the team to address it at once.
scenario: A colleague points urgently to water leaking beside office equipment and asks the team to address it at once.
grammar: Dit is first and vereist second; the required attention is the object. Vereisen means to require. Vereist is the third-person present. Aandacht is an abstract de-word; attributive onmiddellijke takes -e even without an article in this phrase.
variation: Deze fout vereist onmiddellijke aandacht.

dutch: Kom je beloften na.
cue: A colleague reminds you of an agreed commitment while pointing to a task you promised to finish.
scenario: A colleague reminds you of an agreed commitment while pointing to a task you promised to finish.
grammar: The imperative Kom begins the instruction and na closes the separable verb around its object. Nakomen means to fulfil or honour a promise. Je before beloften is possessive, not the subject of a question. Both beloften and beloftes are accepted plurals. The participle is nagekomen.
variation: Kom je afspraken na.

dutch: Je hebt geen verandering aangebracht.
cue: You compare the latest draft with the previous version and point out that no alteration has been made.
scenario: You compare the latest draft with the previous version and point out that no alteration has been made.
grammar: Je is first and hebt second; geen verandering stands inside the perfect-tense bracket before aangebracht. Een verandering aanbrengen means to make a change. Geen negates an indefinite noun phrase. Aanbrengen has participle aangebracht: separable aan plus ge plus irregular bracht. Hebben forms the perfect here.
variation: Je hebt geen wijziging aangebracht.

dutch: Wat is mijn volgende stap na dit sollicitatiegesprek?
english: What's my next step after this job interview?
cue: After a job interview, you ask the interviewer what action you should take next.
scenario: After a job interview, you ask the interviewer what action you should take next.
grammar: Wat is first and is second; the subject is followed by the after-interview phrase. Volgende takes -e before de stap. Sollicitatiegesprek is a het-word and takes dit. Mijn is possessive. Stap is figurative for an action in a process.
variation: Wat is de volgende stap na dit sollicitatiegesprek?

dutch: Ik doe mijn best.
cue: You concentrate on a difficult practical task and reassure a colleague that you are making your strongest effort.
scenario: You concentrate on a difficult practical task and reassure a colleague that you are making your strongest effort.
grammar: Ik is first and doe second; mijn best completes the fixed expression. Je best doen means to make your best effort. Doe is the ik form of doen. Best stays without -e in this expression. The present can describe current effort or a commitment, depending on context.
variation: We doen ons best.

dutch: Ze waren niet in de kamer tijdens het gesprek.
english: They weren't in the room during the conversation.
cue: You explain that two colleagues could not have heard a private conversation because their seats in the room were empty.
scenario: You explain that two colleagues could not have heard a private conversation because their seats in the room were empty.
grammar: Plural Ze is first and waren second; niet negates their being in the room during the conversation. Waren is plural past of zijn. Kamer is a de-word and gesprek a het-word. Tijdens takes a noun phrase. Niet negates the location claim rather than an indefinite object.
variation: Ze waren tijdens het gesprek niet in de kamer.

dutch: Hij was blij met het resultaat.
english: He was happy with the result.
cue: A colleague smiles proudly at the finished piece of furniture he has made.
scenario: A colleague smiles proudly at the finished piece of furniture he has made.
grammar: Hij is first and was second; blij takes the reason for satisfaction with met. Was is singular past of zijn. Blij met expresses satisfaction with a result; blij is predicative without -e. Resultaat is a het-word.
variation: Zij was blij met het resultaat.

dutch: Breng me het geleende gereedschap terug.
english: Bring the borrowed tools back to me.
cue: A person who lent tools asks a colleague to return the tool case after the repair.
scenario: A person who lent tools asks a colleague to return the tool case after the repair.
grammar: Breng starts the instruction; short recipient me precedes the full object, and terug closes the verb. Terugbrengen is separable. Me is an unstressed object pronoun. Gereedschap is an uncountable het-word for tools collectively. Geleende is an attributive participle with -e after definite het.
variation: Breng het geleende gereedschap aan mij terug.

dutch: Wat is de truc om deze knoop los te maken?
english: What's the trick to untying this knot?
cue: You hold a knotted cord and ask a skilled colleague how to loosen it.
scenario: You hold a knotted cord and ask a skilled colleague how to loosen it.
grammar: Wat is first and is second; the subject phrase includes an om te explanation of the trick. Truc means a clever method here, not a hidden disadvantage. Knoop is a de-word and takes deze; it means knot in this context. Losmaken is separable: los te maken. The object precedes that infinitive.
variation: Hoe maak ik deze knoop los?

dutch: Het is tijd om de klanten terug te bellen.
english: It's time to call the customers back.
cue: You set aside other work and reach for the phone to return waiting customers’ calls.
scenario: You set aside other work and reach for the phone to return waiting customers’ calls.
grammar: Het is first and is second; tijd is followed by an om phrase with the customers before terug te bellen. Het is tijd om introduces an action that should now begin. Terugbellen is separable and takes te between terug and bellen. Klanten is plural of klant. Het is a dummy subject, not a particular object.
variation: Het is nu tijd om de klanten terug te bellen.

dutch: Hij is gewend aan zwaar tillen.
cue: An experienced warehouse worker lifts a bulky crate with a practised stance while a colleague watches.
scenario: An experienced warehouse worker lifts a bulky crate with a practised stance while a colleague watches.
grammar: Hij is first and is second; gewend takes the activity with aan. Gewend aan describes familiarity. Tillen is an infinitive used to name an activity after aan. Zwaar modifies the lifting as an adverb, not an adjective before a noun. This is a present state, not a past habit.
variation: Hij is gewend aan het tillen van zware dozen.

dutch: Ze zijn hier voor de rondleiding.
english: They're here for the guided tour.
cue: A small group of visitors has arrived at a museum reception to meet their guide.
scenario: A small group of visitors has arrived at a museum reception to meet their guide.
grammar: Ze is first and plural zijn second; hier gives location and voor names the reason for being there. Plural zijn makes ze mean they. Rondleiding is a de-word and means a guided tour. Voor introduces a noun purpose phrase; it is not the om te construction used before an infinitive.
variation: Ze zijn voor de rondleiding hier.

dutch: Ik denk erover om een bedrijf te starten.
english: I'm thinking about starting a business.
cue: You sketch a possible small-business idea at home while discussing whether to start it.
scenario: You sketch a possible small-business idea at home while discussing whether to start it.
grammar: Ik is first and denk second; erover anticipates the om te phrase explaining what is being considered. Erover refers to the contemplated action, not a place. Denken over is followed here by om plus object and te starten. Bedrijf is a het-word, but indefinite een does not reveal gender. Thinking about it is not a firm decision.
variation: Ik overweeg een bedrijf te starten.

dutch: Ik heb een woordenboek voor je gekocht.
english: I bought a dictionary for you.
cue: You present a newly purchased dictionary to a friend who is learning Dutch.
scenario: You present a newly purchased dictionary to a friend who is learning Dutch.
grammar: Ik is first and heb second; the object and beneficiary are inside the perfect bracket before gekocht. Kopen has irregular participle gekocht and takes hebben in this perfect. Voor je names the person benefiting. Woordenboek is a compound ending in het boek. Je is an object pronoun after voor.
variation: Ik heb dit woordenboek voor je gekocht.

dutch: We zitten boven ons budget.
cue: Two event organisers compare their spending with the funds available and discover they have exceeded their budget.
scenario: Two event organisers compare their spending with the funds available and discover they have exceeded their budget.
grammar: We is first and zitten second; boven ons budget expresses the financial position. Zitten describes being in a situation here, not necessarily physical sitting. Boven means above or beyond the permitted amount. Budget is a het-word, so the possessive is ons, not onze.
variation: We zitten boven het afgesproken budget.

dutch: Het waterpeil stijgt.
cue: You watch water rise against a riverbank and point out the increasing level to a companion.
scenario: You watch water rise against a riverbank and point out the increasing level to a companion.
grammar: The full subject Het waterpeil is first and stijgt second. Waterpeil is a compound het-word for water level. Stijgt is the third-person singular present of stijgen. The present can describe a change happening now; Dutch does not require a progressive auxiliary.
variation: Het waterpeil stijgt snel.

dutch: Dat is genoeg verf voor deze muur.
english: That's enough paint for this wall.
cue: While painting a room, you show that the remaining paint in the tin will cover the wall.
scenario: While painting a room, you show that the remaining paint in the tin will cover the wall.
grammar: Dat is first and is second; genoeg precedes the uncountable material and voor names its use. Genoeg is a quantity word before verf. Verf is uncountable here, with no indefinite article. Muur is a de-word and takes deze. Dat can refer to the amount of paint just shown.
variation: Deze hoeveelheid verf is genoeg voor de muur.

dutch: We verbleven tijdens de conferentie in het hotel.
english: We stayed at the hotel during the conference.
cue: Two conference participants recall their stay beside hotel luggage and conference folders.
scenario: Two conference participants recall their stay beside hotel luggage and conference folders.
grammar: We is first and plural past verbleven second; the conference period precedes the hotel location here. Verblijven has past singular verbleef and plural verbleven. It means to stay temporarily, not to live permanently. Hotel is a het-word. Tijdens is a preposition before a noun, not a conjunction before a clause.
variation: Tijdens de conferentie verbleven we in het hotel.

dutch: Je hebt geen bericht op mijn voicemail achtergelaten.
english: You didn't leave a message on my voicemail.
cue: After a missed call, you explain to the caller that there was no voicemail message to tell you what they needed.
scenario: After a missed call, you explain to the caller that there was no voicemail message to tell you what they needed.
grammar: Je is first and hebt second; the negated message and voicemail phrase precede final achtergelaten. Achterlaten is separable; its participle is achtergelaten with ge between achter and laten. Geen negates an indefinite message. Mijn is possessive. Op mijn voicemail specifies where the message would have been left.
variation: Je hebt op mijn voicemail geen bericht achtergelaten.
