dutch: Laat ze het nieuwe ontwerp zien.
cue: You ask a designer to show a small group the newly finished design drawing.
scenario: You ask a designer to show a small group the newly finished design drawing.
grammar: Laat starts the instruction; short recipient ze comes before the full design object, with zien at the end. Laten zien means to show. Zien is a bare infinitive, without te. Ze is an unstressed object pronoun meaning them here. Ontwerp is a het-word; definite het takes attributive nieuwe with -e.
variation: Laat het nieuwe ontwerp aan hen zien.

dutch: Ik ga in de bibliotheek werken.
english: I'm going to work in the library.
cue: You prepare your laptop and books at a quiet library table before beginning a work session.
scenario: You prepare your laptop and books at a quiet library table before beginning a work session.
grammar: Ik is first and ga second; the library location stands before final werken. Gaan plus an infinitive can express an intention or upcoming action. Werken stays without te. In de bibliotheek says where the work will happen; it does not say that the speaker works as a librarian.
variation: Vandaag ga ik in de bibliotheek werken.

dutch: Onze kookles begint nu.
cue: At a teaching kitchen, the instructor calls the gathered learners to begin preparing ingredients.
scenario: At a teaching kitchen, the instructor calls the gathered learners to begin preparing ingredients.
grammar: The full subject Onze kookles is first and begint second; nu gives the start time. Kookles is a de-word and takes possessive onze. Begint is third-person singular because lesson is singular, even though onze refers to several people. Nu means now.
variation: Nu begint onze kookles.

dutch: Zij heeft de verf voor ons gekocht.
english: She bought the paint for us.
cue: A friend brings the paint she bought for your home-decorating project and gives it to your group.
scenario: A friend brings the paint she bought for your home-decorating project and gives it to your group.
grammar: Zij is first and heeft second; paint and beneficiary are before the final participle. Heeft makes zij singular she. Ons is the object pronoun us after voor, not a possessive before verf. Kopen has participle gekocht. Verf is a de-word for paint.
variation: Ze heeft de verf voor ons gekocht.

dutch: Laten we een beslissing over de vakantiedata nemen.
english: Let's make a decision about the holiday dates.
cue: Two friends compare possible holiday periods and agree that it is time to choose the dates.
scenario: Two friends compare possible holiday periods and agree that it is time to choose the dates.
grammar: Laten we introduces a joint proposal; the full decision phrase comes before final nemen. Een beslissing nemen means to make a decision. Over introduces its topic. Vakantiedata is plural of vakantiedatum, with data meaning dates here, not computer information. Nemen is bare after laten.
variation: Laten we de vakantiedata kiezen.

dutch: Ik heb een pen met blauwe inkt nodig.
english: I need a pen with blue ink.
cue: You need a blue-ink pen to complete a paper form and ask a nearby colleague for one.
scenario: You need a blue-ink pen to complete a paper form and ask a nearby colleague for one.
grammar: Ik is first and heb second; the full requested item stands before nodig. Iets nodig hebben expresses need and is present tense here, not perfect. Met blauwe inkt specifies the pen; blauwe has -e before the de-word inkt. Inkt is uncountable. Nodig is an adjective.
variation: Ik heb een blauwe pen nodig.

dutch: Zal je volgende week vrij zijn om te verhuizen?
english: Will you be free next week to move house?
cue: You ask a friend whether their schedule allows them to move house next week, beside packed boxes.
scenario: You ask a friend whether their schedule allows them to move house next week, beside packed boxes.
grammar: The yes/no question starts with Zal, followed by je; zijn closes the future bracket before the purpose phrase. Both zal je and zul je are standard. Vrij means available here. Zijn is bare after zal; verhuizen takes te in the separate om phrase. Volgende week needs no preposition.
variation: Zul je volgende week vrij zijn om te verhuizen?

dutch: Het recept voor deze soep is simpel.
english: The recipe for this soup is simple.
cue: You show a friend the few basic ingredients needed for an uncomplicated soup recipe.
scenario: You show a friend the few basic ingredients needed for an uncomplicated soup recipe.
grammar: The full recipe phrase is first and is second; simpel is the predicate adjective. Recept is a het-word. Soep is a de-word and takes deze. Simpel after is has no attributive -e. Voor deze soep identifies which recipe is meant.
variation: Dit recept is simpel.

dutch: Laten we kansen voor vrijwilligerswerk identificeren.
english: Let's identify opportunities for volunteer work.
cue: A group compares local community projects to find where they could volunteer.
scenario: A group compares local community projects to find where they could volunteer.
grammar: Laten we introduces the joint proposal; the opportunities phrase precedes final identificeren. Identificeren means to identify or establish which options are available, not yet to choose one. Kansen is plural of kans. Vrijwilligerswerk is an uncountable het-word for volunteer work. No te follows laten.
variation: Laten we mogelijkheden voor vrijwilligerswerk zoeken.

dutch: Ik had het voorbereidende werk al gedaan toen de monteur aankwam.
english: I'd already done the preparatory work when the technician arrived.
cue: You show a technician a workspace that you had already cleared and prepared before their arrival.
scenario: You show a technician a workspace that you had already cleared and prepared before their arrival.
grammar: Had is second in the main clause and gedaan closes its bracket. Toen introduces a past-event clause with final aankwam. Had plus gedaan is past perfect: completion before another past event. Al means already. Voorbereidende takes -e after definite het werk. Aankomen is separable, but its finite verb stays joined at the end of this subordinate clause.
variation: Toen de monteur aankwam, had ik het voorbereidende werk al gedaan.

dutch: Werk je nu aan het verslag van de excursie?
english: Are you working on the report about the excursion now?
cue: You ask a student at a desk whether they are currently writing the report on their class excursion.
scenario: You ask a student at a desk whether they are currently writing the report on their class excursion.
grammar: The yes/no question starts with Werk before subject je; nu and the task phrase follow. When subject je or jij follows the finite present verb, werk has no -t. Werken aan names the task being worked on. Verslag is a het-word; van de excursie specifies the report’s topic.
variation: Ben je nu bezig met het verslag van de excursie?

dutch: Is dat je definitieve antwoord op de uitnodiging?
english: Is that your final answer to the invitation?
cue: You check whether a friend’s decision about an invitation is settled before replying to the organiser.
scenario: You check whether a friend’s decision about an invitation is settled before replying to the organiser.
grammar: The yes/no question begins with Is; dat is subject and the answer phrase follows. Je is possessive before definitieve antwoord. Definitieve takes -e after a possessive, including with het-word antwoord. Antwoord op names what is answered. Definitief means final rather than provisional.
variation: Is dit je definitieve antwoord op de uitnodiging?

dutch: Waar is zijn kantoor in dit gebouw?
english: Where is his office in this building?
cue: At an office-building reception, you ask where a colleague’s office is located.
scenario: At an office-building reception, you ask where a colleague’s office is located.
grammar: Waar is first and is second; zijn kantoor is subject, with the building phrase specifying the search area. Zijn before kantoor is possessive his, not an infinitive. Kantoor and gebouw are het-words; gebouw takes dit. Waar asks for location, not direction.
variation: Waar bevindt zijn kantoor zich in dit gebouw?

dutch: Het onderhoud van deze machine is belangrijk.
english: The maintenance of this machine is important.
cue: You explain the importance of regular maintenance while inspecting a workshop machine with a colleague.
scenario: You explain the importance of regular maintenance while inspecting a workshop machine with a colleague.
grammar: The full maintenance phrase is first and is second; belangrijk gives the judgement. Onderhoud is an uncountable het-word. Van deze machine names what is maintained; machine is a de-word. Belangrijk is predicative without -e. This statement evaluates maintenance, rather than issuing a specific obligation.
variation: Regelmatig onderhoud is belangrijk.

dutch: Ik bel de tandarts na mijn werk terug.
english: I'll call the dentist back after work.
cue: You check a missed call from the dental practice while leaving work and plan to return it afterward.
scenario: You check a missed call from the dental practice while leaving work and plan to return it afterward.
grammar: Ik is first and bel second; the recipient and time phrase come before final terug. Terugbellen is separable. Bel is the ik form. Na mijn werk means after my work period. The present can express a firm near-future intention in this context. Tandarts is a de-word.
variation: Na mijn werk bel ik de tandarts terug.

dutch: We hebben een oplossing voor het opslagprobleem gevonden.
english: We have found a solution to the storage problem.
cue: A team shows newly fitted shelves that solve the shortage of storage space in their room.
scenario: A team shows newly fitted shelves that solve the shortage of storage space in their room.
grammar: We is first and hebben second; the full solution object precedes final gevonden. Vinden has irregular participle gevonden and takes hebben here. Oplossing voor names the problem solved. Opslagprobleem is a compound het-word. The perfect reports a completed discovery, not only the need to find a solution.
variation: We hebben het opslagprobleem opgelost.

dutch: Is de fietsenwinkel op maandag open?
english: Is the bicycle shop open on Mondays?
cue: Outside a bicycle shop with a bicycle to repair, you ask a companion whether it opens on Mondays.
scenario: Outside a bicycle shop with a bicycle to repair, you ask a companion whether it opens on Mondays.
grammar: Is starts the yes/no question; the shop subject is followed by the Monday phrase and open. Fietsenwinkel is a compound de-word. Open is predicative, with no -e. Op maandag can express a recurring Monday schedule in this opening-hours context; it can also mean a specific Monday in other contexts.
variation: Is de fietsenwinkel op maandagen open?

dutch: Het bedrijf heeft zijn beleid bijgewerkt.
english: The company has updated its policy.
cue: An administrator replaces an old company-policy folder with the newly updated version and informs a colleague.
scenario: An administrator replaces an old company-policy folder with the newly updated version and informs a colleague.
grammar: The company subject is first and heeft second; zijn beleid is inside the perfect bracket before bijgewerkt. Bijwerken is separable and has participle bijgewerkt. Bedrijf and beleid are het-words. Zijn refers possessively to the company, meaning its here; grammatical gender does not make the company a person. Beleid is generally uncountable.
variation: Het bedrijf heeft het beleid bijgewerkt.

dutch: Wees slim en vergelijk de prijzen voordat je boekt.
english: Be smart and compare the prices before you book.
cue: Before booking accommodation, you compare several options and encourage a friend to check their prices.
scenario: Before booking accommodation, you compare several options and encourage a friend to check their prices.
grammar: Two imperatives are joined by en; voordat introduces a clause ending in finite boekt. Wees is the irregular imperative of zijn. Slim is predicative without -e. Vergelijk is the imperative stem of vergelijken. In voordat je boekt, subject je precedes boekt, so its -t stays. Prijzen means monetary prices here.
variation: Wees verstandig en vergelijk de prijzen voordat je boekt.
